fields: What is the key distinction between an instruction and a control?
An instruction influences model behavior; a control enforces what the runtime is permitted to do.
Why should team-level Claude configuration be standardized?
Shared guidance, tools, permissions, and Skills reduce inconsistent behavior and operational drift.
What should AI-assisted development optimize?
Developer throughput while preserving independent verification, security boundaries, and human accountability.
How should verification strength change with consequence?
More consequential changes require stronger independent tests, review, and approval.
What is the core operational debugging loop?
Move from symptom to evidence to likely layer to fix to verification.
Why should a runbook include rollback/fallback and an owner?
Operators need safe recovery actions and clear escalation responsibility during incidents.
Instruction
Guidance intended to influence model behavior.
Control
An enforceable runtime, permission, sandbox, policy, or CI boundary.
Verification tool
An independent mechanism such as tests, linters, type checks, security scans, or CI used to check generated changes.
Reviewability
The ability for developers to understand and own an AI-generated change.
Runbook
Documented operational steps for diagnosis, mitigation, rollback/fallback, escalation, and evidence preservation.
“Do not modify production” is an instruction; removing production credentials is an enforceable {{c1::control}}.
Shared Skills and configuration should be {{c1::versioned and reviewed}} like other operational assets.
AI assistance should accelerate the engineering loop, not bypass {{c1::CI, code review, or security boundaries}}.
The more consequential the change, the stronger the {{c1::independent verification}} required.
Operational debugging should proceed from symptom → evidence → likely layer → fix → {{c1::verification}}.
A production incident fix should become a {{c1::regression test}} when possible.
What mechanism enforces what the runtime is permitted to do?
Control
What reusable Anthropic package can contain instructions, scripts, and resources?
Agent Skill
What quality means developers can understand and own an AI-generated change?
Reviewability
What document gives repeatable incident diagnosis and recovery steps?
Runbook
A team tells Claude Code “never touch production,” but every developer environment has production admin credentials. What is strongest?

[{"id":"a","text":"Remove/restrict production credentials and permissions; keep the instruction as supplemental guidance."},{"id":"b","text":"Repeat the instruction more often."},{"id":"c","text":"Disable code review."},{"id":"d","text":"Give the model more context about production."}]
a
Hard permission boundaries should not depend on model compliance.
Each developer has a different MCP/tool configuration and shared workflows behave inconsistently. What should the team do?

[{"id":"a","text":"Standardize high-value repository/team configuration and version it."},{"id":"b","text":"Encourage every developer to improvise permanently."},{"id":"c","text":"Hide configuration from version control."},{"id":"d","text":"Give all developers broader credentials."}]
a
Shared configuration improves reproducibility and governance.
A third-party Skill contains scripts and external resources. What should happen before team-wide adoption?

[{"id":"a","text":"Review provenance/content, test it, and constrain permissions appropriately."},{"id":"b","text":"Trust it because it is called a Skill."},{"id":"c","text":"Give it full production access first."},{"id":"d","text":"Skip review because Skills are only text."}]
a
Skills can affect behavior and execution and should be governed.
Which is an enforceable control rather than an instruction?

[{"id":"a","text":"A sandbox/network policy that prevents access to production."},{"id":"b","text":"A sentence saying “be careful.”"},{"id":"c","text":"A README asking the agent not to deploy."},{"id":"d","text":"A prompt example showing a safe action."}]
a
Enforceable boundaries restrict capability independently of model choice.
An agent writes a large refactor and tests pass, but nobody reviews whether the tests cover the risk. What is missing?

[{"id":"a","text":"Independent human/system verification of both the change and test adequacy."},{"id":"b","text":"A larger model."},{"id":"c","text":"Production credentials."},{"id":"d","text":"Fewer tests."}]
a
Passing tests are evidence, not a substitute for judging whether verification is sufficient.
A developer asks an agent to “make it work” using production admin credentials. What is the strongest correction?

[{"id":"a","text":"Use a scoped development/test environment and require approval for shared/destructive actions."},{"id":"b","text":"Let the agent proceed because the developer asked."},{"id":"c","text":"Disable logs."},{"id":"d","text":"Remove rollback mechanisms."}]
a
Developer productivity should not expand unnecessary production capability.
AI-generated code is merged, but no team member understands it well enough to maintain it. What principle was violated?
[{"id":"a","text":"Reviewability and human accountability for the change."},{"id":"b","text":"Prompt caching."},{"id":"c","text":"Semantic retrieval."},{"id":"d","text":"Model lifecycle."}]
a
Teams must be able to own and maintain generated changes.
Quality drops after a deployment. Which evidence should be checked first?

[{"id":"a","text":"Model/prompt versions, retrieval/index changes, traces, and input-distribution changes around the deployment."},{"id":"b","text":"Only ask the model why it failed."},{"id":"c","text":"Delete old logs."},{"id":"d","text":"Immediately add production admin access."}]
a
Debugging starts from correlated evidence around the affected layer/change.
An agent suddenly receives “permission denied” from a tool. What areas are most relevant?

[{"id":"a","text":"Credentials, scopes, authorization policy, tool contract, and dependency status."},{"id":"b","text":"RAG chunk size only."},{"id":"c","text":"Model temperature only."},{"id":"d","text":"Business ROI only."}]
a
Tool failures should be diagnosed at the integration/permission boundary.

[{"id":"a","text":"As a security incident focused on authorization/filtering boundaries, with containment and evidence preservation."},{"id":"b","text":"As an ordinary style-quality issue."},{"id":"c","text":"By only rewriting the prompt."},{"id":"d","text":"By deleting logs immediately."}]

Order a team enablement flow for a new Claude tool/Skill.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Define the intended team use case"},{"id":"s2","text":"Review provenance and required permissions"},{"id":"s3","text":"Configure the tool/Skill in a scoped environment"},{"id":"s4","text":"Test behavior and controls"},{"id":"s5","text":"Version and roll out the approved configuration"}]
Use case and security review precede scoped rollout.
Order a safe AI-assisted coding loop.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Define the task and acceptance criteria"},{"id":"s2","text":"Let the agent explore/implement within scoped permissions"},{"id":"s3","text":"Run independent automated checks"},{"id":"s4","text":"Review the change and evidence"},{"id":"s5","text":"Merge/deploy through normal controlled processes"}]
AI generation is followed by independent verification and normal release controls.
Order a repeatable incident-resolution loop.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Detect the symptom/alert"},{"id":"s2","text":"Collect correlated evidence"},{"id":"s3","text":"Identify and isolate the likely failing layer"},{"id":"s4","text":"Mitigate/fix with rollback or safe recovery as needed"},{"id":"s5","text":"Verify and add regression coverage"}]
Evidence-driven diagnosis precedes mitigation and regression protection.
